title.en: Volume 100: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Wuluohou
title.raw: 卷100 高句麗 百濟 勿吉 失韋 豆莫婁 地豆于 庫莫奚 契丹 烏洛侯 Volume 100: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Wuluohou

sentences.zh: 高句麗 百濟 勿吉 失韋 豆莫婁 地豆于 庫莫奚 契丹 烏洛侯

translations.literal: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Wuluohou
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Wuluohou

sentences.zh: 高句麗者，出於夫餘，自言先祖朱蒙。

translations.literal: Goguryeo came forth from Buyeo; they themselves say their founding ancestor was Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Goguryeo traced their origin to Buyeo and claimed Jumong as their founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙母河伯女，為夫餘王閉於室中，為日所照，引身避之，日影又逐。

translations.literal: Jumong's mother was a daughter of the River Lord; the King of Buyeo shut her in a room; she was illuminated by the sun; she turned her body to avoid it, but the sun's shadow pursued her again.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong's mother was said to be a daughter of the River Lord. The king of Buyeo had shut her in a chamber, where sunlight fell upon her; she turned away to escape it, yet the sun's shadow followed her still.

sentences.zh: 既而有孕，生一卵，大如五升。

translations.literal: Thereupon she became pregnant and gave birth to an egg as large as five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: She soon conceived and bore an egg as large as a five-sheng measure.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王棄之與犬，犬不食；

translations.literal: The King of Buyeo discarded it for dogs, but the dogs would not eat it;
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo cast it out for the dogs, but they would not touch it;

sentences.zh: 棄之與豕，豕又不食；

translations.literal: he discarded it for pigs, but the pigs would not eat it either;
translations.idiomatic: he gave it to pigs, and they too refused it;

sentences.zh: 棄之於路，牛馬避之；

translations.literal: he discarded it on the road, and oxen and horses avoided it;
translations.idiomatic: he left it on the road, and cattle and horses shunned it;

sentences.zh: 後棄之野，眾鳥以毛茹之。

translations.literal: later he discarded it in the wilderness, and many birds fed it with their feathers.
translations.idiomatic: finally he abandoned it in the wild, where flocks of birds warmed it with their down.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王割剖之，不能破，遂還其母。

translations.literal: The King of Buyeo tried to cut it open but could not break it, so he returned it to its mother.
translations.idiomatic: The king tried to cut the egg open but could not break it, and so returned it to the mother.

sentences.zh: 其母以物裹之，置於暖處，有一男破殼而出。

translations.literal: His mother wrapped it in cloth and placed it in a warm place; a boy broke out of the shell.
translations.idiomatic: She wrapped it in cloth and set it in a warm spot until a boy hatched from the shell.

sentences.zh: 及其長也，字之曰朱蒙，其俗言「朱蒙」者，善射也。

translations.literal: When he grew up, they gave him the style-name Jumong; in their speech 'Jumong' means skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age they styled him Jumong, which in their tongue meant 'skilled archer.'

sentences.zh: 夫餘人以朱蒙非人所生，將有異志，請除之，王不聽，命之養馬。

translations.literal: The people of Buyeo, thinking Jumong was not born of a human and would harbor unusual designs, asked that he be eliminated; the king did not listen and ordered him to raise horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Buyeo believed that Jumong, not born of ordinary men, would prove dangerous, and urged the king to kill him; the king refused and set him to tend horses instead.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙每私試，知有善惡，駿者減食令瘦，駑者善養令肥。

translations.literal: Whenever Jumong tested the horses privately, he knew which were good and which bad; for the swift ones he reduced their feed to make them lean, and for the slow ones he fed them well to make them fat.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong secretly tested the herds and could tell the good from the bad: he cut the rations of swift horses to keep them lean, while he fattened the slow ones with generous feed.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王以肥者自乘，以瘦者給朱蒙。

translations.literal: The King of Buyeo rode the fat horses himself and gave the lean ones to Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: The king kept the fat horses for himself and gave Jumong only the lean ones.

sentences.zh: 後狩于田，以朱蒙善射，限之一矢。

translations.literal: Later when hunting in the fields, because Jumong was skilled at archery, they limited him to one arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a hunt, because Jumong was so fine an archer, they allowed him only a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙雖矢少，殪獸甚多。

translations.literal: Though Jumong had few arrows, he killed many beasts.
translations.idiomatic: With that one shaft he nevertheless brought down a great many animals.

sentences.zh: 夫餘之臣又謀殺之。

translations.literal: The ministers of Buyeo again plotted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of Buyeo again conspired to kill him.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙母陰知，告朱蒙曰：「國將害汝，以汝才略，宜遠適四方。」

translations.literal: Jumong's mother secretly learned of this and told Jumong: 'The state is about to harm you; given your talent and ability, you should go far away to distant lands.'
translations.idiomatic: Jumong's mother learned of the plot in secret and warned him: 'The realm means to destroy you. With your gifts, you should flee far beyond these borders.'

sentences.zh: 朱蒙乃與烏引、烏違等二人，棄夫餘，東南走。

translations.literal: Jumong then, together with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two others, abandoned Buyeo and fled southeast.
translations.idiomatic: So Jumong left Buyeo with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two companions and fled southeast.

sentences.zh: 中道遇一大水，欲濟無梁，夫餘人追之甚急。

translations.literal: On the way they came upon a great river; they wished to cross but there was no bridge; the people of Buyeo pursued them very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Midway they reached a broad river with no bridge, while Buyeo pursuers pressed hard behind them.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙告水曰：「我是日子，河伯外孫，今日逃走，追兵垂及，如何得濟？」

translations.literal: Jumong addressed the water: 'I am the child of the sun, the grandson of the River Lord; today I flee, and the pursuing soldiers are almost upon me—how can I get across?'
translations.idiomatic: Jumong cried to the river: 'I am the child of the sun and grandson of the River Lord. I flee for my life and the pursuers are upon me—how am I to cross?'

sentences.zh: 於是魚鼈並浮，為之成橋，朱蒙得渡，魚鼈乃解，追騎不得渡。

translations.literal: Thereupon fish and turtles all rose to the surface and formed a bridge for him; Jumong was able to cross, and then the fish and turtles dispersed and the pursuing horsemen could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Fish and turtles then rose and formed a living bridge; Jumong crossed safely, the creatures sank away, and the horsemen could not follow.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙遂至普述水，遇見三人，其一人著麻衣，一人著納衣，一人著水藻衣，與朱蒙至紇升骨城，遂居焉，號曰高句麗，因以為氏焉。

translations.literal: Jumong thus reached the Puyeo River, where he met three men—one wearing hemp garment, one wearing coarse cloth garment, and one wearing waterweed garment—and together with Jumong they came to Keshenggu City, settled there, and called themselves Goguryeo; thereby this became their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong came to the Puyeo River and met three men—one in hemp, one in coarse cloth, one in waterweed—and with them he reached Keshenggu, made it his seat, and took the name Goguryeo, which became their clan designation.

sentences.zh: 初，朱蒙在夫餘時，妻懷孕，朱蒙逃後生一子，字始閭諧。

translations.literal: Initially, while Jumong was still in Buyeo, his wife was pregnant; after Jumong fled she gave birth to a son, who was given the style-name Yuri.
translations.idiomatic: While Jumong was still in Buyeo his wife had been with child; after his flight she bore a son styled Yuri.

sentences.zh: 及長，知朱蒙為國主，即與母亡而歸之，名之曰閭達，委之國事。

translations.literal: When he grew up, learning that Jumong had become ruler of a state, he went with his mother to join him; Jumong named him Yuri-da and entrusted him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy grew up and learned that Jumong ruled a kingdom, he went with his mother to join him; Jumong called him Yuri-da and placed the government in his hands.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙死，閭達代立。

translations.literal: When Jumong died, Yuri-da succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jumong's death, Yuri-da took the throne.

sentences.zh: 閭達死，子如栗代立。

translations.literal: When Yuri-da died, his son Yuryu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuri-da was succeeded by his son Yuryu.

sentences.zh: 如栗死，子莫來代立，乃征夫餘，夫餘大敗，遂統屬焉。

translations.literal: When Yuryu died, his son Mare came succeeded; he then campaigned against Buyeo; Buyeo suffered a great defeat and he brought them under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yuryu's son Mare came then reigned, marched against Buyeo, routed it utterly, and brought the kingdom under his sway.

sentences.zh: 莫來子孫相傳，至裔孫宮，生而開目能視，國人惡之。

translations.literal: Mare's descendants succeeded one another down to the distant descendant Gong, who was born with his eyes already open and able to see; the people hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Mare's line held the throne until a distant descendant, Gong, was born with his eyes already open; the people loathed him.

sentences.zh: 及長凶虐，國以殘破。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was fierce and cruel, and the state was reduced to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He grew vicious and cruel, and the realm was brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 宮曾孫位宮亦生而視，人以其似曾祖宮，故名為位宮，高句麗呼相似為「位」。

translations.literal: Gong's great-grandson Weigong was also born able to see; because people thought he resembled his great-grandfather Gong, he was named Weigong; in Goguryeo speech 'wei' means 'to resemble.'
translations.idiomatic: Gong's great-grandson too was born with open eyes; because he seemed to mirror his forebear Gong, he was called Weigong, for in Goguryeo wei means 'to resemble.'

sentences.zh: 位宮亦有勇力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Weigong also had courage and strength and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong was likewise bold and strong, expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 魏正始中，入寇遼西安平，[1]為幽州刺史毋丘儉所破。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei, he invaded Liaoxi and Anping,[1] but was defeated by Muqiu Jian, Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Zhengshi reign he raided Liaoxi and Anping[1] but was crushed by Muqiu Jian, inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 其玄孫乙弗利，利子釗，烈帝時與慕容氏相攻擊。

translations.literal: His distant descendant Isagoru, Isagoru's son Chao, and in the reign of Emperor Lie fought back and forth with the Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: A distant descendant, Isagoru, was followed by his son Chao, who in the reign of Emperor Lie waged war back and forth with the Murong.

sentences.zh: 建國四年，慕容元真率眾伐之，入自南陝，戰於木底，大破釗軍，乘勝長驅，遂入丸都，釗單馬奔竄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuansun led troops to attack him, entering from Nanyang, fought at Mudi, routed Chao's army, pursued at length, entered Wandu, and Chao fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuansun marched against him by way of Nanyang, defeated him at Mudi, swept on in pursuit, and entered Wandu while Chao fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 元真掘釗父墓，載其屍，并掠其母妻、珍寶、男女五萬餘口，焚其宮室，毀丸都城而還。

translations.literal: Yuansun dug up Chao's father's tomb, loaded the corpse, and also seized his mother, wife, treasures, and more than fifty thousand men and women, burned the palaces, destroyed Wandu city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun opened Chao's father's tomb and carried off the corpse, together with Chao's mother and wife, his treasures, and more than fifty thousand captives; he burned the palaces, razed Wandu, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自後釗遣使來朝，阻隔寇讎，不能自達。

translations.literal: Afterward Chao sent envoys to court, but blocked by enemies and feuds, he could not get through on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Chao sent envoys to court, but enemies and feuds barred the way and his missions could not reach us.

sentences.zh: 釗後為百濟所殺。

translations.literal: Later Chao was killed by Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was later killed by Baekje.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，釗曾孫璉始遣使者安東奉表貢方物，并請國諱。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Shizu, Chao's great-grandson Lian first sent the envoy Andong to present a memorial with local products and also requested the taboo names of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Chao's great-grandson Lian first sent the envoy Andong with tribute and a request for the imperial taboo names.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其誠款，詔下帝系名諱於其國，遣員外散騎侍郎李敖拜璉為都督遼海諸軍事、征東將軍、領護東夷中郎將、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was pleased with his sincerity and ordered the imperial genealogy and taboo names sent to their state; he dispatched the Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace Attendant Li Ao to invest Lian as Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Leader for Pacifying the Eastern Yi Middle General, Duke Who Opens the State of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed his loyalty, sent down the imperial genealogy and taboo names, and dispatched Li Ao, supernumerary gentleman of the palace attendant, to invest Lian as commander of all Liaohai forces, general who conquers the east, leader for pacifying the eastern Yi, duke who opens Liaodong commandery, and king of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 敖至其所居平壤城，訪其方事，云：遼東南一千餘里，東至柵城，南至小海，北至舊夫餘，民戶參倍於前。

translations.literal: When Ao reached their capital Pyongyang and inquired about their territory, he was told: more than a thousand li southeast of Liaodong, east to Chasung, south to the lesser sea, north to old Buyeo; households were several times what they had been before.
translations.idiomatic: Ao reached their seat at Pyongyang and asked about their domain: more than a thousand li southeast of Liaodong, east to Chasung, south to the lesser sea, north to old Buyeo, with households several times greater than before.

sentences.zh: 魏時，其地東西二千里，南北一千餘里。

translations.literal: In Wei times their territory was two thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times their land stretched two thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.

sentences.zh: 民皆土著，隨山谷而居，衣布帛及皮。

translations.literal: The people all settled on the land, dwelling along the valleys; they wore cloth, silk, and fur.
translations.idiomatic: The people were all native to the soil, dwelling along the valleys, and dressed in cloth, silk, and fur.

sentences.zh: 土田薄塉，蠶農不足以自供，故其人節飲食。

translations.literal: The soil was thin and poor; sericulture and farming were insufficient for self-supply, so the people were sparing in food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The land was thin and poor; silk and grain could not fully sustain them, so they were frugal in eating and drinking.

sentences.zh: 其俗淫，好歌舞，夜則男女羣聚而戲，無貴賤之節，然潔淨自喜。

translations.literal: Their customs were licentious; they loved songs and dances; at night men and women gathered in groups to play without distinction of noble and base, yet they delighted in cleanliness.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were loose; they loved song and dance, and at night men and women mingled without regard to rank, though they took pride in cleanliness.

sentences.zh: 其王好治宮室。

translations.literal: Their king loved to build palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Their king delighted in building palaces.

sentences.zh: 其官名有謁奢、太奢、大兄、小兄之號。

translations.literal: Their official titles included Yecha, Taisha, Da Xiong, and Xiao Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Their offices bore such titles as yecha, taisha, da xiong, and xiao xiong.

sentences.zh: 頭著折風，其形如弁，旁插鳥羽，貴賤有差。

translations.literal: They wore on the head the 'folded wind,' shaped like a cap, with bird feathers inserted at the side, differing by noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: On their heads they wore the zhefeng, shaped like a cap with bird feathers at the sides, varied according to rank.

sentences.zh: 立則反拱，跪拜曳一脚，行步如走。

translations.literal: When standing they arched backward with hands joined; when kneeling and bowing they dragged one foot; when walking their gait was like running.
translations.idiomatic: Standing, they bowed with hands clasped behind; kneeling, they dragged one foot; walking, they moved as if in a hurry.

sentences.zh: 常以十月祭天，國中大會。

translations.literal: They regularly worshipped Heaven in the tenth month with a great assembly of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the tenth month they worshipped Heaven in a great national assembly.

sentences.zh: 其公會，衣服皆錦繡，金銀以為飾。

translations.literal: At their public assemblies their clothes were all brocade and embroidery, with gold and silver as ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: At their public gatherings all wore brocade and embroidery adorned with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 好蹲踞。

translations.literal: They liked to squat on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: They were fond of squatting on their heels.

sentences.zh: 食用俎几。

translations.literal: They ate using tables and dish-stands.
translations.idiomatic: They ate from tables and stands.

sentences.zh: 出三尺馬，云本朱蒙所乘，馬種即果下也。

translations.literal: They produced horses three feet [tall]—they said these were originally ridden by Jumong; the breed was the 'fruit-beneath' horse.
translations.idiomatic: They bred horses only three feet high, said to be the strain Jumong once rode—the guoxia, or 'dwarf' horse.

sentences.zh: 後貢使相尋，歲致黃金二百斤，白銀四百斤。

translations.literal: Later tributary envoys came in succession, each year presenting two hundred jin of gold and four hundred jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Later their envoys came in steady succession, each year bringing two hundred jin of gold and four hundred jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 時馮文通率眾奔之，世祖遣散騎常侍封撥詔璉令送文通，璉上書稱當與文通俱奉王化，竟不送。

translations.literal: At the time Feng Wentong led his followers and fled to them; Emperor Shizu dispatched the Regular Attendant Feng Bo with an edict ordering Lian to send Wen Tong back; Lian submitted a memorial saying he intended to submit to the royal transformation together with Wen Tong and in the end did not deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Wentong fled to them with his followers, Emperor Shizu sent Feng Bo with orders to hand him over; Lian replied that he and Wen Tong would together accept royal rule, yet in the end he did not surrender him.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，欲往討之，樂平王丕等議待後舉，世祖乃止，而文通亦尋為璉所殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was angry and wished to go punish them; the Prince of Leping Wang Pi and others advised waiting for a later expedition, so the emperor stopped; before long Wen Tong was also killed by Lian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and meant to march against them, but the Prince of Leping and others urged delay, and he desisted; before long Lian had Wen Tong killed as well.

sentences.zh: 後文明太后以顯祖六宮未備，敕璉令薦其女。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Wenming, because Emperor Xianzu's six palaces were not yet complete, ordered Lian to recommend his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Emperor Xianzu's inner palaces were not yet filled, Empress Dowager Wenming ordered Lian to present his daughter.

sentences.zh: 璉奉表，云女已出嫁，求以弟女應旨，朝廷許焉，乃遣安樂王真、尚書李敷等至境送幣。

translations.literal: Lian submitted a memorial saying his daughter had already married and asked to send his younger brother's daughter in fulfillment of the order; the court consented and dispatched the Prince of Anle Wang Zhen, Minister Li Fu, and others to the border to deliver betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Lian reported that his daughter was already married and offered his younger brother's daughter instead; the court agreed and sent the Prince of Anle and Minister Li Fu to the border with betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 璉惑其左右之說，云朝廷昔與馮氏婚姻，未幾而滅其國，殷鑒不遠，宜以方便辭之。

translations.literal: Lian was swayed by those around him who said that in the past when the court had married with the Feng clan it had not been long before that state was destroyed—a recent warning was not far off, and he should politely decline by some expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was persuaded by his advisers that when the court had once married a Feng princess, that house was soon destroyed—a lesson not far in the past—and that he should find some polite excuse to refuse.

sentences.zh: 璉遂上書妄稱女死。

translations.literal: Lian then falsely submitted a memorial claiming his daughter had died.
translations.idiomatic: Lian then falsely reported that the girl had died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑其矯詐，又遣假散騎常侍程駿切責之，若女審死者，聽更選宗淑。

translations.literal: The court suspected this deception and again sent the Acting Regular Attendant Cheng Jun to rebuke him sternly, saying that if the daughter were truly dead they might select another clanswoman of noble birth.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspected fraud and sent Acting Regular Attendant Cheng Jun to rebuke him sharply, adding that if she were truly dead they might choose another noble clanswoman.

sentences.zh: 璉云：「若天子恕其前愆，謹當奉詔。」

translations.literal: Lian said: 'If the Son of Heaven will forgive my former fault, I shall respectfully obey the edict.'
translations.idiomatic: Lian replied: 'If the Son of Heaven will forgive my earlier offense, I shall respectfully obey.'

sentences.zh: 會顯祖崩，乃止。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Xianzu died, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: But Emperor Xianzu died just then, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 至高祖時，璉貢獻倍前，其報賜亦稍加焉。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozu, Lian's tribute doubled what it had been, and his rewards in return were also somewhat increased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozu, Lian's tribute doubled, and the gifts returned to him were increased as well.

sentences.zh: 時光州於海中得璉所遣詣蕭道成使餘奴等送闕，高祖詔責璉曰：「道成親殺其君，竊號江左，朕方欲興滅國於舊邦，繼絕世於劉氏，而卿越境外交，遠通篡賊，豈是藩臣守節之義！

translations.literal: At that time Guang Province at sea captured envoys sent by Lian to Xiao Daocheng, including Yu Nu and others, and sent them to the capital; Emperor Gaozu issued an edict rebuking Lian: 'Daocheng personally killed his sovereign and usurped the title on the left bank of the river; I am about to restore a destroyed state to its old homeland and continue the interrupted line of the Liu house—and you cross borders in foreign relations and communicate with a usurping rebel far away—is this the loyal conduct proper to a frontier subject!
translations.idiomatic: Guang Province then seized at sea envoys Lian had sent to Xiao Daocheng, including Yu Nu, and sent them to court. Emperor Gaozu rebuked Lian: 'Daocheng murdered his own ruler and usurped the throne south of the river. I mean to restore a fallen state and continue the Liu line—yet you traffic across borders with a distant rebel. Is this how a frontier vassal should keep faith?

sentences.zh: 今不以一過掩卿舊款，即送還藩，其感恕思愆，祗承明憲，輯寧所部，動靜以聞。」

translations.literal: Now I shall not let one fault cover your past loyalty; return speedily to your fief; be grateful for this forgiveness, reflect on your errors, respectfully receive the bright statutes, bring peace to your domain, and report your movements.'
translations.idiomatic: I will not let this one lapse efface your former loyalty. Return at once to your fief, be grateful for forgiveness, ponder your fault, obey the imperial statutes, keep your domain in order, and report all you do.'

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，璉死，年百餘歲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, Lian died at over a hundred years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, Lian died at more than a hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉哀於東郊，遣謁者僕射李安上策贈車騎大將軍、太傅、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu held mourning in the eastern suburb and dispatched the Court Gentleman Attendant Li An to present a funeral offering conferring the posthumous title Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, Duke Who Opens the State of Liaodong Commandery, King of Goguryeo, with the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu mourned him in the eastern suburb and sent Li An, director of court gentlemen, with funeral gifts conferring grand general of chariots and cavalry, grand tutor, duke who opens Liaodong, and king of Goguryeo, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 又遣大鴻臚拜璉孫雲使持節、都督遼海諸軍事、征東將軍、領護東夷中郎將、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，賜衣冠服物車旗之飾，又詔雲遣世子入朝，令及郊丘之禮。

translations.literal: He also dispatched the Grand Herald to invest Lian's grandson Yun as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Liaohai Military Affairs, General Who Conquers the East, Leader for Pacifying Eastern Yi Middle General, Duke Who Opens Liaodong, King of Goguryeo, granting robes, caps, chariots, banners and other insignia; he also ordered Yun to send his heir to court in time for the suburban and mound rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the grand herald to invest Lian's grandson Yun with the same ranks and insignia, and ordered Yun to send his heir to court for the suburban and mound ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 雲上書辭疾，惟遣其從叔升于隨使詣闕，嚴責之。

translations.literal: Yun submitted a memorial pleading illness and only sent his father's younger brother cousin Shengyu with the envoy to court; they sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun pleaded illness and sent only his cousin Shengyu with the embassy; the court rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 自此歲常貢獻。

translations.literal: From then on tribute was presented every year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute came every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 正始中，世宗於東堂引見其使芮悉弗，[2]悉弗進曰：「高麗係誠天極，累葉純誠，地產土毛，無愆王貢。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, Emperor Shizong received their envoy Ruixifu in the eastern hall;[2] Ruixifu advanced and said: 'Goryeo ties its sincerity to heaven's pole through many generations of pure loyalty; the land produces local products without failing in royal tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Emperor Shizong received their envoy Ruixifu in the eastern hall.[2] Ruixifu said: 'Goryeo has bound its loyalty to the throne for generations; our land yields its native goods and we have never failed in tribute.

sentences.zh: 但黃金出自夫餘，珂則涉羅所產。

translations.literal: But gold comes from Buyeo and ke shells from Sheluo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our gold came from Buyeo and our ke shells from Sheluo.

sentences.zh: 今夫餘為勿吉所逐，涉羅為百濟所并，國王臣雲惟繼絕之義，悉遷于境內。

translations.literal: Now Buyeo has been driven out by Wuji and Sheluo annexed by Baekje; our king subject Yun, moved only by the principle of continuing extinguished lines, has relocated them all within our borders.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo has now been driven out by Wuji and Sheluo swallowed by Baekje; our king Yun, honoring the duty to preserve fallen lines, has taken them all within our borders.

sentences.zh: 二品所以不登王府，實兩賊是為。」

translations.literal: The reason second-grade tribute does not reach the imperial storehouse is truly because of these two enemies.'
translations.idiomatic: It is solely because of these two foes that second-grade tribute no longer reaches the imperial treasury.'

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「高麗世荷上將，專制海外，九夷黠虜，實得征之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said: 'Goryeo through the ages has borne the burden of your generals and ruled the seas exclusively; among the nine Yi and crafty barbarians they can indeed be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'Goryeo has long borne imperial commission and ruled the eastern seas; among the nine Yi and cunning tribes you may indeed chastise them.

sentences.zh: 瓶罄罍耻，誰之咎也？

translations.literal: When the flask is empty the jar is shamed—whose fault is that?
translations.idiomatic: When the lesser vessel is empty, the greater is shamed—whose fault is that?

sentences.zh: 昔方貢之愆，責在連率。

translations.literal: In former times when tribute from the regions was deficient, the blame lay with the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In former days, when regional tribute fell short, the fault lay with the regional commander.

sentences.zh: 卿宜宣朕旨於卿主，務盡威懷之略，揃披害羣，輯寧東裔，使二邑還復舊墟，土毛無失常貢也。」

translations.literal: You should proclaim my intent to your lord: devote yourself to the policy of combining might and kindness, sweep away harms to the masses, bring peace to the eastern lands, and restore the two territories to their old sites so that local products need not fail in regular tribute.'
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim my will to your king: use both force and kindness, clear away those who harm the people, bring peace to the eastern lands, restore the two territories to their old seats, and see that tribute flows as before.'

sentences.zh: 神龜中，雲死，靈太后為舉哀於東堂，遣使策贈車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era Yun died; Empress Ling held mourning in the eastern hall and sent envoys with funeral offering conferring Grand General Chariots and Cavalry, Leader for Pacifying Eastern Yi Commandant, Duke Who Opens Liaodong, King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengui, Yun died; Empress Ling mourned him in the eastern hall and sent funeral gifts conferring grand general of chariots and cavalry, leader for pacifying the eastern Yi, duke who opens Liaodong, and king of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 又拜其世子安為安東將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: She also invested his heir An as General of Pacifying the East, Leader for Pacifying Eastern Yi Commandant, Duke Who Opens Liaodong, King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: She also invested his heir An as general of pacifying the east, leader for pacifying the eastern Yi, duke who opens Liaodong, and king of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 正光初，光州又於海中執得蕭衍所授安寧東將軍衣冠劍佩，及使人江法盛等，送於京師。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguang era Guang Province again seized at sea the robes, sword and belt conferred by Xiao Yan as General of Pacifying the East, and envoys including Jiang Fasheng, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguang, Guang Province again seized at sea the robes, sword, and belt that Xiao Yan had granted An as general of pacifying the east, together with the envoy Jiang Fasheng and others, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 安死，子延立。

translations.literal: When An died, his son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When An died, his son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，詔加延使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，賜衣冠服物車旗之飾。

translations.literal: In the early reign of Emperor Chu, an edict added to Yan's titles Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Grand General Chariots and Cavalry, Leader Eastern Yi Commandant, Duke Who Opens Liaodong, King of Goguryeo, granting robes, insignia, chariots and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Chu, Yan was further invested as bearer of the staff, regular attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, leader for pacifying the eastern Yi, duke who opens Liaodong, and king of Goguryeo, with robes, insignia, chariots, and banners.

sentences.zh: 天平中，詔加延侍中、驃騎大將軍，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era an edict added Attendant-in-Chief and General of Agile Cavalry, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was further made attendant-in-chief and general of agile cavalry, his other titles remaining as before.

sentences.zh: 延死，子成立。

translations.literal: When Yan died, his son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died, his son Cheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 訖於武定末，其貢使無歲不至。

translations.literal: Through the end of Wuding their tributary envoys came every single year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the end of Wuding their envoys came every year without exception.

sentences.zh: 百濟國，其先出自夫餘。

translations.literal: The state of Baekje—its founders also came from Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Baekje likewise traced its origin to Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 其國北去高句麗千餘里，處小海之南。

translations.literal: Their state was more than a thousand li north from Goguryeo, situated south of the lesser sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm lay more than a thousand li south of Goguryeo, on the southern shore of the lesser sea.

sentences.zh: 其民土著，地多下濕，率皆山居。

translations.literal: Their people settled on the land; the terrain was mostly low and wet; they generally dwelt in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were native to the soil; the land was low and damp, and they mostly lived in the hills.

sentences.zh: 有五穀，其衣服飲食與高句麗同。

translations.literal: They had the five grains; their clothing and food were the same as Goguryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: They grew the five grains, and their dress and diet were the same as Goguryeo's.

sentences.zh: 延興二年，其王餘慶始遣使上表曰：「臣建國東極，豺狼隔路，雖世承靈化，莫由奉藩，瞻望雲闕，馳情罔極。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxing their king Yu Qing first sent envoys with a memorial saying: 'Your servant founded a state at the eastern extremity; wolves and jackals block the road; though I inherit spiritual transformation generation after generation I cannot serve as a vassal; gazing toward the cloud gate my yearning has no limit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanxing their king Yu Qing first sent envoys with a memorial: 'Your servant has built a realm at the eastern edge of the world; wolves and jackals bar the road. Though we have long received your transforming grace, we have had no way to serve as vassals. Gazing toward the clouded gate, our longing knows no bound.

sentences.zh: 涼風微應，伏惟皇帝陛下協和天休，不勝係仰之情，謹遣私署冠軍將軍、駙馬都尉弗斯侯，長史餘禮，龍驤將軍、帶方太守、司馬張茂等投舫波阻，搜徑玄津，託命自然之運，遣進萬一之誠。

translations.literal: With the cool wind slightly responding—may Your Majesty the Emperor harmonize with heaven's blessings—unable to bear the feeling of being tied in admiration, I respectfully dispatch my private secretariat General of Victorious Armies, Commandant of the Horse Equipage Marquis Fusi Hou, Chief Clerk Yu Li, General of the Soaring Dragon, Governor of Daifang and Marshal Zhang Mao and others, trusting to the waves to cross barriers, seeking a route through the dark ford, relying on the luck of natural forces to present one ten-thousandth of sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: As the autumn wind stirs, may Your Majesty harmonize with heaven's favor. Unable to contain our reverence, I send my general Fusi Hou, chief clerk Yu Li, and marshal Zhang Mao, governor of Daifang, to cast their boats upon the waves, thread the dark straits, trust to heaven's fortune, and offer this ten-thousandth part of our loyalty.

sentences.zh: 冀神祇垂感，皇靈洪覆，克達天庭，宣暢臣志，雖旦聞夕沒，永無餘恨。」

translations.literal: I hope the divine powers will show feeling and imperial spirit broadly cover, that I may reach the heavenly court and express my subject's will—though I hear of it in the morning and die in the evening, I shall have no remaining regret.'
translations.idiomatic: May the spirits look with favor and imperial grace cover us, that we may reach your court and declare our will—even if we hear your reply at dawn and die at dusk, we shall have no regret.'

sentences.zh: 又云：「臣與高句麗源出夫餘，先世之時，篤崇舊款。

translations.literal: They also said: 'Your servant and Goguryeo both spring from Buyeo; in generations past we held deep to old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'Goguryeo and we both spring from Buyeo; in former ages we held fast to old friendship.

sentences.zh: 其祖釗輕廢隣好，親率士眾，陵踐臣境。

translations.literal: Their ancestor Chao lightly abandoned neighborly goodwill and personally led his troops to trample your servant's borders.
translations.idiomatic: Their ancestor Chao lightly cast aside neighborly ties and led his army in person to trample our borders.

sentences.zh: 臣祖須整旅電邁，應機馳擊，矢石暫交，梟斬釗首。

translations.literal: Your servant's ancestor mustered his forces like lightning and struck as opportunity allowed; arrows and stones briefly exchanged, and Chao's head was taken and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: My ancestor Xu gathered his troops like lightning, struck when the moment allowed, and after a brief clash took Chao's head and displayed it.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，莫敢南顧。

translations.literal: Since then none has dared look southward.
translations.idiomatic: Since then none has dared turn south against us.

sentences.zh: 自馮氏數終，餘燼奔竄，醜類漸盛，遂見陵逼，構怨連禍，三十餘載，財殫力竭，轉自孱踧。

translations.literal: Since the Feng clan's fate ended their remnants fled in panic; ugly factions gradually grew strong and we came to be oppressed; grievances piled up with calamities for more than thirty years; wealth and strength exhausted, we became ever more weak and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of the Feng house their remnants fled to us; vile enemies grew strong and pressed upon us. For more than thirty years grievance piled on calamity until our wealth and strength were spent and we grew ever weaker.

sentences.zh: 若天慈曲矜，遠及無外，速遣一將，來救臣國，當奉送鄙女，執掃後宮，并遣子弟，牧圉外廐。

translations.literal: If Heaven's compassion bends with mercy, reaching far to none excluded, swiftly send one general to rescue your servant's state—I shall present my humble daughters to sweep the rear palace and send my sons and younger kin to tend the outer stables.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's mercy bends to pity all within the four seas, send a general at once to save my kingdom. I shall offer my humble daughters to serve in the inner palace and send my sons and younger kin to care for your outer stables.

sentences.zh: 尺壤匹夫不敢自有。」

translations.literal: Not an inch of soil nor a single commoner would your servant dare claim as his own.'
translations.idiomatic: Not a foot of ground nor a single subject would I hold for myself.'

sentences.zh: 又云：「今璉有罪，國自魚肉，大臣強族，戮殺無已，罪盈惡積，民庶崩離。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Now Lian is guilty; the state itself is fish and meat; great ministers and powerful clans slaughter without end; crimes overflow and evils accumulate; the common people scatter and fall apart.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'King Lian is now guilty of crimes. The kingdom is being carved up like fish on a board; powerful ministers and great clans slaughter without cease. His crimes overflow and his wickedness piles high, and the common people are breaking away.

sentences.zh: 是滅亡之期，假手之秋也。

translations.literal: This is the season of extinction, the autumn for lending a hand.
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour of their destruction—the moment to strike through another's hand.

sentences.zh: 且馮族士馬，有鳥畜之戀；

translations.literal: Moreover the Feng clan's warriors and horses have the attachment of birds and penned beasts;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Feng clan's soldiers and horses still yearn for their homeland like caged birds and penned beasts;

sentences.zh: 樂浪諸郡，懷首丘之心。

translations.literal: the commanderies of Lelang harbor hearts longing for their old mound.
translations.idiomatic: the old Lelang commanderies still yearn for their ancestral home.

sentences.zh: 天威一舉，有征無戰。

translations.literal: When Heaven's majesty is raised once, there is expedition without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once your celestial might moves, you shall campaign without needing to fight.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不敏，志效畢力，當率所統，承風響應。

translations.literal: Your servant though not clever aspires to exhaust all strength; I shall lead those I command to answer in echo to the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not clever, I am resolved to give all my strength and to lead my forces to follow your banner.

sentences.zh: 且高麗不義，逆詐非一，外慕隗囂藩卑之辭，內懷兇禍豕突之行。

translations.literal: Moreover Goguryeo is unrighteous; rebellion and deception are not once; outwardly they admire Kui Xiao's words of vassal humility; inwardly they harbor vicious calamity and boar-rush conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo is faithless, and their treachery knows no end. Outwardly they mimic Kui Xiao's humble words of submission; inwardly they nurse violent schemes like a boar charging its pen.

sentences.zh: 或南通劉氏，或北約蠕蠕，共相脣齒，謀陵王略。

translations.literal: Sometimes they ally south with the Liu clan, sometimes covenant north with Rouran, mutual lip and teeth, scheming to encroach on royal dominion.
translations.idiomatic: They traffic south with the Liu house and north with the Rouran, each other's lip to tooth, plotting to violate imperial sway.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯至聖，致罰丹水；

translations.literal: In antiquity Tang Yao the supremely sage inflicted punishment on the Dan River tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Even Tang Yao in his supreme sagacity punished the Dan River people;

sentences.zh: 孟常稱仁，不捨塗詈。

translations.literal: Meng Chang was called benevolent yet did not spare the man who reviled on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius was praised for humanity yet did not spare the insulter on the highway.

sentences.zh: 涓流之水，宜早壅塞，今若不取，將貽後悔。

translations.literal: Trickling water should be blocked early; if you do not seize now, you will leave regret behind.
translations.idiomatic: A trickle ought to be dammed early; fail to act now and regret will follow.

sentences.zh: 去庚辰年後，臣西界小石山北國海中見屍十餘，并得衣器鞍勒，視之非高麗之物，後聞乃是王人來降臣國。

translations.literal: After the year gengchen, on your servant's western border at Little Stone Mountain in the northern state's sea I saw more than ten corpses, and also obtained clothing, implements, saddle and bridle; viewing them they were not Goguryeo goods; later I heard they were the Great King's men coming to surrender to your servant's state.
translations.idiomatic: After the gengchen year, on the northern sea off my western border at Little Stone Mountain we found more than a dozen corpses along with clothing, gear, and saddlery that were plainly not Goguryeo goods. We later learned they were your envoys seeking refuge in my kingdom.

sentences.zh: 長蛇隔路，以沉于海，雖未委當，深懷憤恚。

translations.literal: The long serpent blocked the road and they sank into the sea; though the matter is not yet verified, I harbor deep indignation.
translations.idiomatic: That long serpent barred their way and drowned them in the sea. Though the facts are not yet settled, my anger runs deep.

sentences.zh: 昔宋戮申舟，楚莊徒跣；

translations.literal: In antiquity Song killed Shen Zhou; King Zhuang of Chu went barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: When Song killed Shen Zhou, King Zhuang of Chu went barefoot in grief;

sentences.zh: 鷂撮放鳩，信陵不食。

translations.literal: an osprey seized and released a dove; Lord Xinling refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: when an osprey seized a dove, Lord Xinling would not eat—for he had shown mercy.

sentences.zh: 克敵建名，美隆無已。

translations.literal: Defeating the enemy and establishing a name—glory mounts without end.
translations.idiomatic: To defeat the foe and win a name is glory that knows no end.

sentences.zh: 夫以區區偏鄙，猶慕萬代之信，況陛下合氣天地，勢傾山海，豈令小竪，跨塞天逵。

translations.literal: That such a tiny remote petty place still cherishes faith for ten thousand generations—how much more Your Majesty who joins qi with heaven and earth, whose power tilts mountains and seas—would you allow a petty fellow to straddle and block the heavenly thoroughfare?
translations.idiomatic: If even our poor remote corner still hopes for a promise to last ten thousand generations, how much more should you, who unite your breath with heaven and earth and whose might overtops mountains and seas, suffer a petty rogue to block the road to the throne?

sentences.zh: 今上所得鞍一，以為實驗。」

translations.literal: The saddle Your Majesty has now received—take it as proof.'
translations.idiomatic: The saddle we now present is offered as proof.'

sentences.zh: 顯祖以其僻遠，冒險朝獻，禮遇優厚，遣使者邵安與其使俱還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu, because of their remoteness and their braving danger to come to court with tribute, treated them with generous courtesy and sent the envoy Shao An to return together with their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu, moved by their distant realm and the risks they took to present tribute, received them with exceptional courtesy and sent the envoy Shao An to escort their party home.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得表聞之，無恙甚善。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Receiving your memorial and hearing of it—you are without affliction; very good.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 'I have received your memorial and am glad to learn that you are well.

sentences.zh: 卿在東隅，處五服之外，不遠山海，歸誠魏闕，欣嘉至意，用戢于懷。

translations.literal: You are in the eastern corner, situated outside the five zones; not distant from mountains and seas, returning in sincerity to Wei's gate-tower; I rejoice and praise your utmost intent and gather it into my breast.
translations.idiomatic: You stand at the eastern edge, beyond the five zones, yet not far from mountain and sea you have turned in loyalty to the Wei court. I rejoice in your utmost sincerity and hold it close in my heart.

sentences.zh: 朕承萬世之業，君臨四海，統御羣生。

translations.literal: I inherit the enterprise of ten thousand generations, face all within the four seas as lord, and govern all living beings.
translations.idiomatic: I have inherited an empire meant to last ten thousand generations, rule over the four seas, and govern all living things.

sentences.zh: 今宇內清一，八表歸義，襁負而至者不可稱數，風俗之和，士馬之盛，皆餘禮等親所聞見。

translations.literal: Now within the four seas all is pure; the eight directions return to righteousness; those carried on the back to come cannot be counted; the harmony of customs and the abundance of soldiers and horses—all Yu Li and the rest have personally heard and seen.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is united and the eight directions submit; envoys arrive in numbers beyond count. Yu Li and his companions have themselves witnessed the peace of our customs and the strength of our armies.

sentences.zh: 卿與高麗不穆，屢致陵犯，苟能順義，守之以仁，亦何憂於寇讎也。

translations.literal: You and Goguryeo are not harmonious and repeatedly incur violation and encroachment; if you can accord with righteousness and guard with benevolence, what worry need you have of enemy foes?
translations.idiomatic: You and Goguryeo are at odds and they have repeatedly encroached upon you; if you uphold righteousness and govern with humanity, what need have you to fear your enemies?

sentences.zh: 前所遣使，浮海以撫荒外之國，從來積年，往而不返，存亡達否，未能審悉。

translations.literal: The envoys formerly sent, crossing the sea to comfort states beyond the wilds—for many years since they went without return—whether they live or die, succeed or fail—I have not been able to examine and know fully.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys I once sent across the sea to reach the outer lands have been gone for years without return, and I have been unable to learn whether they live or die, or whether they ever arrived.

sentences.zh: 卿所送鞍，比校舊乘，非中國之物。

translations.literal: The saddle you sent—comparing it with old mounts—is not an article of the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: The saddle you sent, when compared with our usual tack, is plainly not of Central States manufacture.

sentences.zh: 不可以疑似之事，以生必然之過。

translations.literal: One must not from suspicious matters give rise to a necessarily fixed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: One must not turn suspicion alone into a settled charge of guilt.

sentences.zh: 經略權要，已具別旨。」

translations.literal: The strategic essentials of planning authority have already been set forth in separate instructions.'
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of strategy have been set forth in separate instructions.'

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「知高麗阻強，侵軼卿土，修先君之舊怨，棄息民之大德，兵交累載，難結荒邊。

translations.literal: Another edict said: 'Knowing Goguryeo obstructs with strength and invades and overruns your lands, nursing old grievances of former rulers, abandoning the great virtue of giving the people rest, arms clashing for accumulated years—it is hard to settle the wild border.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict said: 'I know that Goguryeo blocks your way with force, raids your territory, nurses old feuds from former kings, and abandons the great virtue of giving the people peace. Years of fighting have made the frontier hard to settle.

sentences.zh: 使兼申胥之誠，國有楚越之急，乃應展義扶微，乘機電舉。

translations.literal: Causing you to combine Shen Xu's sincerity—the state has Chu-Yue urgency—one ought then to extend righteousness and support the weak, seizing the moment like lightning to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Your plight is like Wu Zixu's loyalty or the urgency of Chu and Yue; it would be right to extend righteousness, aid the weak, and strike like lightning when the moment comes.

sentences.zh: 但以高麗稱藩先朝，供職日久，於彼雖有自昔之釁，於國未有犯令之愆。

translations.literal: But Goguryeo has called itself vassal to the former court and performed duties for a long day; toward them though there are ancient quarrels, toward the state there has been no offense violating orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Goguryeo has long called itself a vassal of the former court and performed its duties. Though you have old grievances against them, they have committed no breach of imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 卿使命始通，便求致伐，尋討事會，理亦未周。

translations.literal: Your mission has just begun communication and you immediately request to launch attack—searching the considerations of affairs, the principle is also not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your envoys have only just opened relations, yet you already ask for an expedition. On reflection, the matter is not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 故往年遣禮等至平壤，欲驗其由狀。

translations.literal: Therefore in former years I sent Li and others to Pyongyang, wishing to verify the origins and circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I sent Yu Li and his party to Pyongyang last year to verify the facts.

sentences.zh: 然高麗奏請頻煩，辭理俱詣，行人不能抑其請，司法無以成其責，故聽其所啟，詔禮等還。

translations.literal: Yet Goguryeo's memorial requests were frequent and troublesome; their rhetoric and reasoning both were well-attuned; the envoys could not suppress their pleas; the judicial office had no way to fulfill the charge—therefore I heeded what they reported and ordered Li and others to return.
translations.idiomatic: But Goguryeo petitioned repeatedly with polished arguments; our envoys could not refuse their pleas, and the judicial office could not fix guilt upon them. I therefore accepted their account and ordered Yu Li's party to return.

sentences.zh: 若今復違旨，則過咎益露，後雖自陳，無所逃罪，然後興師討之，於義為得。

translations.literal: If now they again disobey the edict, then fault and guilt will be the more exposed; afterward though they plead for themselves there is nowhere to escape punishment—then raising troops to chastise them will be proper in principle.
translations.idiomatic: If they now defy the edict again, their guilt will stand revealed; even if they plead later, they cannot escape punishment. Then to raise an army against them will be justified.

sentences.zh: 九夷之國，世居海外，道暢則奉藩，惠戢則保境，故羈縻著於前典，楛貢曠於歲時。

translations.literal: The states of the nine yi dwell beyond the sea for generations; when the Way is open they serve as vassals, when favor rests they guard their borders—therefore restraint-and-attachment is recorded in former canons, and tribute of huo-sticks is absent for years at a time.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of the nine yi have always lived beyond the sea: when the Way prevails they submit as vassals; when grace rests upon them they guard their borders. Hence the classics record them under restraint-and-attachment, and their tribute of huo-arrows may lapse for years.

sentences.zh: 卿備陳強弱之形，具列往代之迹，俗殊事異，擬貺乖衷，洪規大略，其致猶在。

translations.literal: You have fully set forth the form of strong and weak, completely listed the traces of past generations; customs differ and affairs differ; your analogies miss the mark—yet the grand plan's great outline, its attainment still remains.
translations.idiomatic: You have fully described their strength and weakness and traced the record of past ages. Customs differ and circumstances differ, so some of your comparisons miss the mark—yet the broad outline of the grand design still holds.

sentences.zh: 今中夏平一，宇內無虞，每欲陵威東極，懸旌域表，拯荒黎於偏方，舒皇風於遠服。

translations.literal: Now the Central Xia is unified and peaceful; within the four seas no worry; every time I wish to let majesty overrun the eastern extremity, hang banners beyond the borders, rescue wild multitudes in remote corners, and spread imperial wind over distant domains.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Central Lands are united and the realm is at peace. I have long wished to extend my majesty to the eastern edge, plant my banners beyond the borders, rescue the wild peoples of remote corners, and spread imperial grace over distant lands.

sentences.zh: 良由高麗即敍，未及卜征。

translations.literal: Truly because Goguryeo now keeps order, I have not yet reached the time to divine expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Goguryeo has lately kept the peace have I not yet chosen a day for campaign.

sentences.zh: 今若不從詔旨，則卿之來謀，載協朕意，元戎啟行，將不云遠。

translations.literal: If now they do not follow the edict's intent, then your coming stratagem fully accords with my mind; the main army will set out, and it will not be said to be far.
translations.idiomatic: If they now disobey the edict, your proposal will fully accord with my intent, and the main army will march—not far off.

sentences.zh: 便可豫率同興，具以待事，時遣報使，速究彼情。

translations.literal: You may then beforehand lead together in rising, prepare fully to await the affair, and from time to time send reporting envoys to speedily investigate their situation.
translations.idiomatic: You may then muster your forces in advance, make ready for action, and send envoys from time to time to report swiftly on their conduct.

sentences.zh: 師舉之日，卿為鄉導之首，大捷之後，又受元功之賞，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: On the day the army is raised, you shall be chief of guides; after great victory you shall again receive reward for supreme merit—is it not good?
translations.idiomatic: When the army marches, you shall lead the guides; after a great victory you shall receive the highest reward. Would that not be well?

sentences.zh: 所獻錦布海物雖不悉達，明卿至心。

translations.literal: The brocade, cloth, and sea-products you presented, though not all arrived, clearly show your utmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though not all the brocade, cloth, and sea-products you sent have reached us, your utmost sincerity is clear.

sentences.zh: 今賜雜物如別。」

translations.literal: Now gifts of miscellaneous goods are given as specified separately.'
translations.idiomatic: Gifts of various goods are now bestowed as set forth in the accompanying list.'

sentences.zh: 又詔璉護送安等。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Lian to escort An and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered King Lian to escort Shao An and his party.

sentences.zh: 安等至高句麗，璉稱昔與餘慶有讎，不令東過，安等於是皆還。

translations.literal: When An and the others reached Goguryeo, Lian claimed that in the past he had a feud with Yu Qing and would not let them pass east; An and the others then all returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao An and his party reached Goguryeo, King Lian claimed an old feud with Yu Qing and refused to let them pass eastward. Shao An and the others therefore all turned back.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔切責之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued sternly reproaching him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict sternly rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 五年，使安等從東萊浮海，賜餘慶璽書，褒其誠節。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he sent An and others from Donglai by sea, bestowing on Yu Qing imperial written credentials and praising his sincerity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he sent Shao An and his party by sea from Donglai, bestowing on Yu Qing an imperial letter of credence and praising his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 安等至海濱，遇風飄蕩，竟不達而還。

translations.literal: An and the others reached the seashore, encountered wind and drifted, and in the end did not reach their destination and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shao An and his party reached the coast, were blown about by storms, and in the end failed to arrive and turned back.

sentences.zh: 勿吉國，在高句麗北，舊肅慎國也。

translations.literal: The state of Wuji is north of Goguryeo; it is the old state of Sushen.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Wuji lay north of Goguryeo; it was the old land of Sushen.

sentences.zh: 邑落各自有長，不相總一。

translations.literal: Settlements each have their own chiefs and are not united under one.
translations.idiomatic: Each settlement had its own chief and they were not united under a single ruler.

sentences.zh: 其人勁悍，於東夷最強。

translations.literal: Their people are fierce and stalwart; among the Eastern Yi they are strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were fierce and stalwart—the strongest among the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 言語獨異。

translations.literal: Their language is uniquely different.
translations.idiomatic: Their language was wholly distinct.

sentences.zh: 常輕豆莫婁等國，諸國亦患之。

translations.literal: They constantly look down on Doumolou and other states; the various states also suffer from them.
translations.idiomatic: They constantly looked down on Doumolou and other states, and those states likewise feared them.

sentences.zh: 去洛五千里。

translations.literal: Five thousand li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lay five thousand li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自和龍北二百餘里有善玉山，山北行十三日至祁黎山，又北行七日至如洛瓌水，水廣里餘，又北行十五日至太魯水，又東北行十八日到其國。

translations.literal: From two hundred-odd li north of Helong is Mount Shanyu; thirteen days' travel north from the mountain reaches Mount Qili; seven days further north reaches the Ruluogui River, more than one li wide; fifteen days further north reaches the Tailu River; eighteen days northeast reaches their state.
translations.idiomatic: Some two hundred li north of Helong stood Mount Shanyu; thirteen days' march north of it brought one to Mount Qili, and seven days further north to the Ruluogui River, over a li wide. Fifteen days north lay the Tailu River, and eighteen days northeast brought one to their country.

sentences.zh: 國有大水，闊三里餘，名速末水。

translations.literal: The state has a great river more than three li wide, named the Summo River.
translations.idiomatic: Within the country ran a great river more than three li across, called the Summo River.

sentences.zh: 其地下濕，築城穴居，屋形似塚，開口於上，以梯出入。

translations.literal: The ground is wet and low; they build walled pit dwellings; houses resemble mounds with openings above, entering and exiting by ladder.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low and damp; they built walled pit dwellings whose roofs resembled burial mounds, with openings above and ladders for entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 其國無牛，有車馬，佃則偶耕，車則步推。

translations.literal: Their state has no cattle; they have carts and horses; in tilling they pair-plow; for carts they push on foot.
translations.idiomatic: They had no cattle but did have carts and horses; they plowed in pairs, and pushed their carts by hand.

sentences.zh: 有粟及麥穄，菜則有葵。

translations.literal: They have millet and chaff of wheat; for vegetables there is mallow.
translations.idiomatic: They grew millet and wheat, and among vegetables they had mallow.

sentences.zh: 水氣醎凝，鹽生樹上，亦有鹽池。

translations.literal: Water-vapor brine condenses; salt grows on trees; there are also salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: Brine condensed from the damp air; salt formed on trees, and there were salt ponds as well.

sentences.zh: 多猪無羊。

translations.literal: Many pigs, no sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They kept many pigs but had no sheep.

sentences.zh: 嚼米醞酒，飲能至醉。

translations.literal: They chew rice to ferment wine; drinking it they can reach intoxication.
translations.idiomatic: They chewed rice to brew wine, and a draught of it could bring intoxication.

sentences.zh: 婦人則布裙，男子猪犬皮裘。

translations.literal: Women wear cloth skirts; men wear pig and dog fur coats.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore cloth skirts; men wore coats of pig and dog hide.

sentences.zh: 初婚之夕，男就女家執女乳而罷，便以為定，仍為夫婦。

translations.literal: On the first night of marriage the man goes to the woman's house, grasps the woman's breast and stops—that is taken as fixed, and they become husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night the man went to the woman's house, took her breast in his hand, and with that the marriage was fixed and they became husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 俗以人溺洗手面。

translations.literal: The custom is to wash hands and face with human urine.
translations.idiomatic: It was their custom to wash hands and face with human urine.

sentences.zh: 頭插虎豹尾。

translations.literal: They insert tiger and leopard tails in their hair.
translations.idiomatic: They wore tiger and leopard tails in their hair.

sentences.zh: 善射獵，弓長三尺，箭長尺二寸，以石為鏃。

translations.literal: Skilled at shooting and hunting; bows three feet long, arrows one foot two inches, with stone arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled archers and hunters; their bows were three feet long, their arrows a foot and two inches, with stone points.

sentences.zh: 其父母春夏死，立埋之，冢上作屋，不令雨濕；

translations.literal: When their parents die in spring or summer they bury them promptly, build a house atop the mound, and do not let rain wet them;
translations.idiomatic: When parents died in spring or summer they buried them at once, built a shelter over the mound, and kept the rain off;

sentences.zh: 若秋冬，以其屍捕貂，貂食其肉，多得之。

translations.literal: if in autumn or winter they use the corpse to catch sable—the sable eat the flesh and they obtain many.
translations.idiomatic: if in autumn or winter they used the corpse to trap sable—the sable ate the flesh and they caught many.

sentences.zh: 常七八月造毒藥傅箭鏃，射禽獸，中者便死，煮藥毒氣亦能殺人。

translations.literal: They constantly in the seventh or eighth month make poison medicine to smear on arrowheads and shoot birds and beasts; those hit die at once; boiling the medicine, its poisonous vapor can also kill people.
translations.idiomatic: Each seventh or eighth month they made poison, smeared it on arrowheads, and shot game; whatever was struck died at once, and the fumes from boiling the poison could kill a man.

sentences.zh: 國南有徒太山，魏言「大白」，有虎豹羆狼害人，人不得山上溲汙，行逕山者，皆以物盛。

translations.literal: South of the state is Mount Taitai—in Wei speech 'Great White'—with tigers, leopards, bears, and wolves harming people; people must not relieve themselves on the mountain; those traveling by paths on the mountain all use vessels to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the country stood Mount Taitai—'Great White' in Wei speech—where tigers, leopards, bears, and wolves harmed people. No one might relieve himself on the mountain; travelers carried vessels for that purpose.

sentences.zh: 去延興中，遣使乙力支朝獻。

translations.literal: In the Yanxing era they sent the envoy Yili Zhi as tribute to court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era they sent the envoy Yili Zhi to present tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 太和初，又貢馬五百匹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe they again presented five hundred horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe reign they again presented five hundred horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 乙力支稱：初發其國，乘船泝難河西上，至太𣳅河，沉船於水，南出陸行，渡洛孤水，從契丹西界達和龍。

translations.literal: Yili Zhi said: When we first set out from our state we took boats up the Nahan River westward to the Tailu River, sank the boats in the water, went south overland, crossed the Luogu River, and from the western border of the Khitan reached Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Yili Zhi reported: 'When we first left our country we sailed up the Nahan River westward to the Tailu River, scuttled our boats, marched south overland, crossed the Luogu River, and reached Helong by way of the Khitan western frontier.'

sentences.zh: 自云其國先破高句麗十落，密共百濟謀從水道并力取高句麗，遣乙力支奉使大國，請其可否。

translations.literal: They themselves said their state had first broken ten settlements of Goguryeo, secretly together with Baekje plotted by water route to combine strength and take Goguryeo, and sent Yili Zhi to serve as envoy to the great state to ask whether it may proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He said their state had already overrun ten Goguryeo settlements and had secretly joined Baekje in a plan to strike Goguryeo by sea; Yili Zhi had been sent to the great state to ask whether this might be done.

sentences.zh: 詔敕三國同是藩附，宜共和順，勿相侵擾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered: the three states are alike vassal attachments; they should together harmonize and accord; do not mutually invade and harass.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that all three states were imperial vassals and should live in harmony and not attack one another.

sentences.zh: 乙力支乃還。

translations.literal: Yili Zhi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yili Zhi then returned home.

sentences.zh: 從其來道，取得本船，汎達其國。

translations.literal: Following their coming route, they recovered their original boat and floated to reach their state.
translations.idiomatic: He retraced his route, recovered their original boats, and sailed back to his country.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣使侯尼支朝獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year they again sent the envoy Houni Zhi as tribute to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they again sent the envoy Houni Zhi to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年復入貢。

translations.literal: The next year they again entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 其傍有大莫盧國、覆鍾國、莫多回國、庫婁國、素和國、具弗伏國、[3]匹黎尒國、拔大何國、[4]郁羽陵國、庫伏真國、魯婁國、羽真侯國，前後各遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: Beside them are the states of Damolu, Fuzhong, Moduohui, Kulou, Suhe, Jufufu, Pilier, Badah, Yuyuling, Kufuzhen, Lulou, and Yuzhenhou; each in turn sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby lay the states of Damolu, Fuzhong, Moduohui, Kulou, Suhe, Jufufu, Pilier, Badah, Yuyuling, Kufuzhen, Lulou, and Yuzhenhou, each of which sent envoys to court with tribute in its turn.

sentences.zh: 太和十二年，勿吉復遣使貢楛矢方物於京師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe Wuji again sent envoys presenting huo-arrows and local products at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taihe Wuji again sent envoys to the capital with huo-arrows and local products.

sentences.zh: 十七年，又遣使人婆非等五百餘人朝獻。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year they again sent the envoy Ren Pofei and more than five hundred others as tribute to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year they sent the envoy Ren Pofei and more than five hundred others to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，復遣使俟力歸等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming they again sent the envoy Houligui and others as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingming they again sent the envoy Houligui and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 自此迄于正光，貢使相尋。

translations.literal: From this until Zhengguang, tribute envoys followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the Zhengguang era, tribute envoys came in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 爾後，中國紛擾，頗或不至。

translations.literal: After that China was in turmoil and often they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward China fell into turmoil and their missions often failed to arrive.

sentences.zh: 興和二年六月，遣使石久云等貢方物，至於武定不絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xinghe they sent envoys Shi Jiuyun and others with tribute goods; until Wuding they did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Xinghe they sent envoys led by Shi Jiuyun with local products, and tribute continued without break until the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 失韋國，在勿吉北千里，去洛六千里。

translations.literal: The state of Shiwei is a thousand li north of Wuji, six thousand li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Shiwei lay a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 路出和龍北千餘里，入契丹國，又北行十日至啜水，又北行三日有蓋水，又北行三日有犢了山，其山高大，周回三百餘里，又北行三日有大水名屈利，又北行三日至刃水，又北行五日到其國。

translations.literal: The route goes out more than a thousand li north of Helong, enters Khitan territory, ten days north reaches the Chuo River, three days north there is the Gai River, three days north there is Mount Duliao—its mountain lofty and great, circling more than three hundred li—three days north there is a great river named Quli, three days north reaches the Ren River, five days north reaches their state.
translations.idiomatic: The road ran more than a thousand li north of Helong into Khitan country, then ten days north to the Chuo River, three days north to the Gai River, and three days north to lofty Mount Duliao, which circled more than three hundred li. Three days north lay the great Quli River, three days further north the Ren River, and five days north brought one to Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 有大水從北而來，廣四里餘，名㮈水。

translations.literal: A great river comes from the north, more than four li wide, named the Na River.
translations.idiomatic: A great river flowed down from the north, more than four li across, called the Na River.

sentences.zh: 國土下濕。

translations.literal: The national territory is low and wet.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low and damp.

sentences.zh: 語與庫莫奚、契丹、豆莫婁國同。

translations.literal: Their language is the same as Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Doumolou.
translations.idiomatic: Their language was the same as that of the Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Doumolou.

sentences.zh: 頗有粟麥及穄，唯食猪魚，養牛馬，俗又無羊。

translations.literal: They rather have millet, wheat, and kaoliang; they eat only pork and fish, raise cattle and horses; the custom also has no sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They grew millet, wheat, and kaoliang, ate chiefly pork and fish, and raised cattle and horses; like Wuji, they kept no sheep.

sentences.zh: 夏則城居，冬逐水草。

translations.literal: In summer they dwell in walled settlements; in winter they follow water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they lived in walled settlements; in winter they followed the pastures.

sentences.zh: 亦多貂皮。

translations.literal: They also have many sable pelts.
translations.idiomatic: They also had many sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 丈夫索髮。

translations.literal: Husbands wear their hair loose.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore their hair loose.

sentences.zh: 用角弓，其箭尤長。

translations.literal: They use horn bows; their arrows are especially long.
translations.idiomatic: They used horn bows, and their arrows were especially long.

sentences.zh: 女婦束髮，作叉手髻。

translations.literal: Women bind their hair and make crossed-hands buns.
translations.idiomatic: Women bound their hair and wore it in the crossed-hands bun.

sentences.zh: 其國少竊盜，盜一徵三，殺人者責馬三百匹。

translations.literal: In their state there are few thieves; for one theft one is taxed threefold; a murderer is fined three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Theft was rare in their country; a single theft drew a threefold penalty, and murder carried a fine of three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 男女悉衣白鹿皮襦袴。

translations.literal: Men and women alike all wear white deer-skin jackets and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike dressed in jackets and trousers of white deerskin.

sentences.zh: 有麴釀酒。

translations.literal: They have grain mash for brewing wine.
translations.idiomatic: They brewed wine from grain mash.

sentences.zh: 俗愛赤珠，為婦人飾，穿挂於頸，以多為貴，女不得此，乃至不嫁。

translations.literal: The custom loves red pearls as women's ornaments, strung and hung at the neck; the more the more honored; a woman who does not obtain these may even remain unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: They prized red pearls as women's ornaments, strung about the neck—the more the better—and a woman without them might not marry at all.

sentences.zh: 父母死，男女眾哭三年，屍則置於林樹之上。

translations.literal: When parents die, men and women all weep in a crowd for three years; the corpse is then placed atop forest trees.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, men and women wailed together for three years, then set the body on the forest trees.

sentences.zh: 武定二年四月，始遣使張焉豆伐等獻其方物，迄武定末，貢使相尋。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding, fourth month, they first sent envoys Zhang Yandoufa and others to present their regional products; down to the end of Wuding, tribute envoys followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Wuding they first sent envoys such as Zhang Yandoufa with local products; tribute missions continued without break until the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 豆莫婁國，在勿吉國北千里，去洛六千里，舊北扶餘也。

translations.literal: The state of Doumolou is a thousand li north of Wuji, six thousand li from Luoyang; it was formerly Northern Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: Doumolou lay a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang; it had once been Northern Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 在失韋之東，東至於海，方二千里。

translations.literal: East of Shiwei, east reaching the sea, two thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: It lay east of Shiwei, extending east to the sea, about two thousand li on a side.

sentences.zh: 其人土著，有宮室倉庫。

translations.literal: Its people are settled on the land; they have palaces and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: The people were sedentary and had dwellings and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 多山陵廣澤，於東夷之域最為平敞。

translations.literal: Many hills, mounds, and broad marshes; among the Eastern Yi lands it is the most level and open.
translations.idiomatic: The land had many hills and broad marshes, yet among the Eastern Yi it was the most level and open.

sentences.zh: 地宜五穀，不生五果。

translations.literal: The land suits the five grains; the five fruits do not grow.
translations.idiomatic: The soil supported the five grains but not orchard fruits.

sentences.zh: 其人長大，性強勇，謹厚，不寇抄。

translations.literal: Its people are tall and large, by nature strong and brave, careful and simple, and do not raid or plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They were tall and sturdy, brave yet sober and honest, and did not raid their neighbors.

sentences.zh: 其君長皆以六畜名官，邑落有豪帥。

translations.literal: Their lords and chiefs all use the six domestic animals to name offices; settlements have powerful leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs named offices after the six kinds of livestock, and each settlement had its powerful headmen.

sentences.zh: 飲食亦用俎豆。

translations.literal: In eating and drinking they also use stands and platters.
translations.idiomatic: They ate with stands and platters as well.

sentences.zh: 有麻布衣，制類高麗而幅大，其國大人，以金銀飾之。

translations.literal: They have hemp cloth garments, cut like Goguryeo's but broader in the bolt; the great men of the state ornament them with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: They wove hemp cloth in a Goguryeo style but wider in the bolt, and their leading men trimmed it with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 用刑嚴急，殺人者死，沒其家人為奴婢。

translations.literal: They apply punishments strictly and urgently; murderers die, and their household members are seized as male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment was harsh: murderers were put to death and their families enslaved.

sentences.zh: 俗淫，尤惡妬婦，妬者殺之，尸其國南山上至腐。

translations.literal: The custom is licentious; they especially hate jealous wives; jealous ones are killed, the corpse placed on the southern mountain of the state until it rots.
translations.idiomatic: Lust ran deep in their customs, and jealous wives were especially hated—they were executed and left on the southern hill until the flesh rotted away.

sentences.zh: 女家欲得，輸牛馬乃與之。

translations.literal: If the bride's family desires it, cattle and horses are delivered and only then is she given.
translations.idiomatic: The bride's family demanded cattle and horses before the match was granted.

sentences.zh: 或言本穢貊之地也。

translations.literal: Some say it was originally the land of the Yemaek.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that this had been Yemaek territory in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 地豆于國，[5]在失韋西千餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Didouyu is more than a thousand li west of Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Didouyu lay more than a thousand li west of Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 多牛羊，出名馬，皮為衣服，無五穀，惟食肉酪。

translations.literal: Many cattle and sheep, famous horses, skins for clothing, no five grains—only meat and curdled milk are eaten.
translations.idiomatic: They kept great herds and famed horses, dressed in hides, grew no grain, and lived on meat and dairy.

sentences.zh: 延興二年八月，遣使朝貢，至于太和六年，貢使不絕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanching, eighth month, they sent envoys to pay court tribute; down to the sixth year of Taihe, tribute envoys did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Yanching they first sent tribute envoys, and missions continued until the sixth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 十四年，頻來犯塞，高祖詔征西大將軍、陽平王頤擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they repeatedly came to invade the borders; Gaozu decreed that the General Who Conquers the West, the Prince of Yangping, Yi, should attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they raided the frontier repeatedly, until Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Yangping, Yi, general who conquers the west, to drive them away.

sentences.zh: 自後時朝京師，迄武定末，貢使不絕。

translations.literal: From then on they sometimes came to court at the capital; down to the end of Wuding, tribute envoys did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they periodically appeared at court, and tribute missions continued until the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚國之先，東部宇文之別種也。

translations.literal: The Kumo Xi state in antiquity was a separate branch of the Eastern Bulge of the Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Kumo Xi were originally a branch of the Yuwen of the eastern regions.

sentences.zh: 初為慕容元真所破，遺落者竄匿松漠之間。

translations.literal: At first they were broken by Murong Yuansun; those left behind fled and hid in the Pine Desert.
translations.idiomatic: They were first shattered by Murong Yuansun, and survivors hid in the Pine Desert.

sentences.zh: 其民不潔淨，而善射獵，好為寇鈔。

translations.literal: Its people are not clean, yet excel at archery and hunting, and love to act as raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people cared little for cleanliness, were skilled hunters and archers, and delighted in raiding.

sentences.zh: 登國三年，太祖親自出討，至弱洛水南，大破之，獲其四部落，馬牛羊豕十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dengguo, Taizu personally went out to attack; reaching south of the Ruoluo River, he routed them greatly, captured their four tribes, and obtained more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, sheep, and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dengguo Emperor Taizu marched in person to the south bank of the Ruoluo River and crushed them, taking four tribes and more than a hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此羣狄諸種不識德義，互相侵盜，有犯王略，故往征之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "These many Di peoples and various kinds do not know virtue and righteousness; they invade and steal from one another; some violate the royal design, therefore I went to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "These barbarian peoples know neither virtue nor duty; they prey on one another, and when they offend against the realm, I must campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 且鼠竊狗盜，何足為患。

translations.literal: Moreover, rats stealing and dogs thieving—how can they be worth troubling over as a calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Mere rat-and-dog pilfering is scarcely worth a full campaign.

sentences.zh: 今中州大亂，吾先平之，然後張其威懷，則無所不服矣。」

translations.literal: Now the central provinces are in great disorder; I shall first pacify that, then extend my authority and kindness, and then none will fail to submit."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain is in turmoil; I shall settle that first, then extend authority and grace—and nothing will remain unsubdued."

sentences.zh: 既而車駕南還雲中，懷服燕趙。

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial carriage returned south to Yunzhong; Yan and Zhao submitted in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor returned south to Yunzhong, and Yan and Zhao submitted in heart.

sentences.zh: 十數年間，諸種與庫莫奚亦皆滋盛。

translations.literal: Within a dozen or so years, the various kinds together with Kumo Xi all likewise flourished and grew abundant.
