translations.idiomatic: Within a dozen years the frontier peoples, Kumo Xi among them, all grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 及開遼海，置戍和龍，諸夷震懼，各獻方物。

translations.literal: When Liaohai was opened and garrisons were set at Helong, the many Yi were shaken and afraid, each presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao coast was opened and garrisons placed at Helong, the tribes were awed and sent their tribute.

sentences.zh: 高宗、顯祖世，庫莫奚歲致名馬文皮。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Gaozong and Xianzu, Kumo Xi yearly presented famous horses and patterned pelts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Gaozong and Xianzu the Kumo Xi presented famous horses and fine furs annually.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu, they sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Gaozu they sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，輒入塞內，辭以畏地豆于鈔掠，詔書切責之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe they promptly entered within the passes, excusing themselves on grounds of fear of Didouyu's raiding and plundering; an imperial edict sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe they entered the borders, pleading fear of Didouyu raids; the court answered with a sharp reprimand.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入寇安州，營燕幽三州兵數千人擊走之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year they entered to raid Anzhou; troops of several thousand from the three prefectures of Ying, Yan, and You struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year they raided Anzhou until several thousand troops from Ying, Yan, and You drove them off.

sentences.zh: 後復款附，每求入塞，與民交易。

translations.literal: Later they again came sincerely to submit, each time seeking to enter the passes to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: They later submitted again and repeatedly asked to enter the borders to trade with Chinese settlers.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔曰：「庫莫奚去太和二十一年以前，與安營二州邊民參居，交易往來，並無疑貳。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong's edict said: "Kumo Xi, before the twenty-first year of Taihe, lived mingled with the border people of the two prefectures of An and Ying, trading back and forth, with no suspicion or disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong decreed: "Before the twenty-first year of Taihe the Kumo Xi mingled with settlers on the An and Ying frontiers and traded freely, without any breach of trust.

sentences.zh: 至二十二年叛逆以來，遂爾遠竄。

translations.literal: From the twenty-second year, when they rebelled, they thereupon fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Since their rebellion in the twenty-second year they have fled far away.

sentences.zh: 今雖款附，猶在塞表，每請入塞與民交易。

translations.literal: Now although they have come sincerely to submit, they are still beyond the passes, each time requesting to enter the passes to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though they have submitted again, they remain beyond the passes and repeatedly ask to enter and trade with our people.

sentences.zh: 若抑而不許，乖其歸向之心；

translations.literal: If we restrain and do not permit it, we go against their heart of turning toward us;
translations.idiomatic: To refuse them outright would alienate their goodwill;

sentences.zh: 聽而不虞，或有萬一之警。

translations.literal: if we listen and do not guard against it, there may be one chance in ten thousand of an alarm.
translations.idiomatic: yet to allow them without precaution might invite trouble.

sentences.zh: 不容依先任其交易，事宜限節，交市之日，州遣上佐監之。」

translations.literal: It is not permissible to follow the former practice and let them trade freely; the matter should be limited and regulated; on the day of the exchange market, the prefecture shall send a senior aide to supervise it."
translations.idiomatic: They may no longer trade as freely as before: markets shall be regulated, and on trading days each prefecture shall send a senior official to supervise."

sentences.zh: 自是已後，歲常朝獻，至於武定末不絕。

translations.literal: From then on they yearly presented tribute at court; down to the end of Wuding it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent annual tribute without break until the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 契丹國，在庫莫奚東，異種同類，俱竄於松漠之間。

translations.literal: The state of Khitan is east of Kumo Xi; a different kind but the same category; both fled and hid in the Pine Desert.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan state lay east of the Kumo Xi; though a distinct people, they were kin, and both had taken refuge in the Pine Desert.

sentences.zh: 登國中，國軍大破之，遂逃迸，與庫莫奚分背。

translations.literal: In the Dengguo period the imperial army routed them greatly; they thereupon fled in flight and parted from Kumo Xi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dengguo era the imperial army crushed them, and they fled, separating from the Kumo Xi.

sentences.zh: 經數十年，稍滋蔓，有部落，於和龍之北數百里，多為寇盜。

translations.literal: After several decades they gradually spread and multiplied; they had tribes several hundred li north of Helong, and mostly acted as raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few decades they grew again into tribes several hundred li north of Helong and largely took to raiding.

sentences.zh: 真君以來，求朝獻，歲貢名馬。

translations.literal: From Zhenjun onward they sought to present tribute at court and yearly presented famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenjun era onward they sought audience at court and sent famous horses each year.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，使莫弗紇何辰奉獻，得班饗於諸國之末。

translations.literal: In the time of Xianzu, the envoy Mohefu He Chen presented tribute and was ranked to feast among the states at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu the envoy Mohefu He Chen brought tribute and was seated at the feast among the tributary states, though in the lowest place.

sentences.zh: 歸而相謂，言國家之美，心皆忻慕，於是東北羣狄聞之，莫不思服。

translations.literal: Returning, they said to one another, speaking of the state's beauty; all their hearts rejoiced and admired; thereupon the many Di of the northeast heard of it, and none failed to think of submitting.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they spoke among themselves of the splendor of the realm, and every heart was filled with longing; when word spread among the northeastern tribes, all wished to submit.

sentences.zh: 悉萬丹部、何大何部、伏弗郁部、羽陵部、[6]日連部、匹絜部、黎部、[7]吐六于部等，[8]各以其名馬文皮入獻天府，遂求為常。

translations.literal: The Xiwan Dan tribe, He Dahe tribe, Fufu Yu tribe, Yuling tribe, Rilian tribe, Pijie tribe, Li tribe, Tuliuyu tribe, and others each with their famous horses and patterned pelts entered to present to the Heavenly Storehouse, and then sought to make it regular.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiwan Dan, He Dahe, Fufu Yu, Yuling, Rilian, Pijie, Li, Tuliuyu, and other branches each sent famous horses and fine furs to the imperial treasury and asked to do so regularly.

sentences.zh: 皆得交市於和龍、密雲之間，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: All were able to exchange markets between Helong and Miyun; tribute and presentation did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: They were allowed to trade between Helong and Miyun, and their tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，高句麗竊與蠕蠕謀，欲取地豆于以分之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, Goguryeo secretly plotted with the Rouran, wishing to seize Didouyu and divide it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe Goguryeo secretly conspired with the Rouran to seize Didouyu and divide it between them.

sentences.zh: 契丹懼其侵軼，其莫弗賀勿于率其部落車三千乘、眾萬餘口，驅徙雜畜，求入內附，止於白狼水東。

translations.literal: The Khitan feared their invasion and harassment; their Mohefu He Wuyu led their tribes—three thousand carts and more than ten thousand persons—driving and moving mixed livestock, seeking to enter and attach inward, stopping east of the White Wolf River.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing attack, the Khitan chief He Wuyu led his people—three thousand carts and more than ten thousand souls—with their herds to seek refuge within the borders, settling east of the White Wolf River.

sentences.zh: 自此歲常朝貢。

translations.literal: From this time they yearly presented tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they sent tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 後告饑，高祖矜之，聽其入關市糴。

translations.literal: Later they reported famine; Gaozu pitied them and permitted them to enter the passes to buy grain in the markets.
translations.idiomatic: When famine was reported later, Emperor Gaozu took pity and allowed them to enter the passes to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 及世宗、肅宗時，恒遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: By the times of Shizong and Suzong, they constantly sent envoys to present regional products.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Shizong and Suzong they regularly sent envoys with local products.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，契丹使人祖真等三十人還，靈太后以其俗嫁娶之際，以青氊為上服，人給青氊兩匹，賞其誠款之心，餘依舊式。

translations.literal: In the Xiping period, when the Khitan envoys Zu Zhen and thirty others returned, Empress Dowager Ling, because in their custom at marriage they use blue felt as upper garments, gave each person two bolts of blue felt to reward their sincere and submissive hearts; the rest followed the former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era, when thirty Khitan envoys led by Zu Zhen were returning home, Empress Dowager Ling—knowing that blue felt was their finest dress for weddings—gave each man two bolts of blue felt to honor their loyalty; other gifts followed the usual scale.

sentences.zh: 朝貢至齊受禪常不絕。

translations.literal: Court tribute down to Qi receiving the abdication constantly did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute missions continued without break even through Qi's accession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 烏洛侯國，在地豆于之北，去代都四千五百餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Wuluohou is north of Didouyu, more than four thousand five hundred li from the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wuluohou lay north of Didouyu, more than four thousand five hundred li from the capital at Dai.

sentences.zh: 其土下濕，多霧氣而寒，民冬則穿地為室，夏則隨原阜畜牧。

translations.literal: Its soil is low and damp, with much mist and cold; the people in winter bore into the earth for rooms, in summer follow hills and mounds to pasture livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low and damp, misty and cold; in winter the people dug pit dwellings, and in summer they grazed their herds on the uplands.

sentences.zh: 多豕，有穀麥。

translations.literal: Many pigs; they have grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They kept many pigs and grew grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 無大君長，部落莫弗皆世為之。

translations.literal: There is no great lord or chief; tribal Mohefu are all hereditary in office.
translations.idiomatic: They had no paramount chief; each tribe's Mohefu held office by hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 其俗繩髮，皮服，以珠為飾。

translations.literal: Their custom is to bind the hair with cord, wear leather garments, and use pearls as ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: They bound their hair with cord, dressed in hides, and adorned themselves with pearls.

sentences.zh: 民尚勇，不為姦竊，故慢藏野積而無寇盜。

translations.literal: The people esteem bravery and do not commit theft or robbery; therefore goods are carelessly stored in the open fields yet there are no raiding thieves.
translations.idiomatic: The people valued courage and did not steal, so goods were left piled in the open without fear of bandits.

sentences.zh: 好獵射。

translations.literal: They love hunting and archery.
translations.idiomatic: They were fond of hunting and archery.

sentences.zh: 樂有箜篌，木槽革面而施九弦。

translations.literal: In music they have the konghou harp; a wooden trough with leather face and nine strings set upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Their music included the konghou harp, with a wooden frame, leather sounding board, and nine strings.

sentences.zh: 其國西北有完水，東北流合于難水，其地小水皆注於難，東入于海。

translations.literal: Northwest of their state is the Wan River; flowing northeast it joins the Nanshui; the small waters of their land all pour into the Nan and east enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of their country lay the Wan River, which flowed northeast to join the Nan; lesser streams all fed the Nan and ran east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 又西北二十日行有于巳尼大水，所謂北海也。

translations.literal: Again, twenty days' travel northwest there is the great Yusini water, what is called the Northern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days' journey northwest lay the great Yusini waters—the Northern Sea.

sentences.zh: 世祖真君四年來朝，稱其國西北有國家先帝舊墟，石室南北九十步，東西四十步，高七十尺，室有神靈，民多祈請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenjun, Shizu came to court, saying that northwest of their state was the old site of the state's founding emperor—a stone chamber ninety paces north-south, forty paces east-west, seventy chi high; the chamber has a spirit, and the people often pray and request.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenjun they came to court and reported that northwest of their land stood a stone hall on the site of an ancient imperial sanctuary—ninety paces north to south, forty east to west, seventy chi high—a place of numinous power where the people often prayed.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣中書侍郎李敞告祭焉，刊祝文於室之壁而還。

translations.literal: Shizu sent Palace Secretariat Vice Director Li Chang to announce the sacrifice there, carved the prayer text on the chamber's wall, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Chang to offer sacrifice there, inscribed a prayer on the chamber wall, and returned.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夷狄之於中國，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Yi and Di toward China are only to be held by bridle and halter.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Toward China the barbarian peoples were to be held only by loose reins.

sentences.zh: 高麗歲修貢職，東藩之冠，榮哀之禮，致自天朝，亦為優矣。

translations.literal: Goguryeo yearly maintained tribute duties, crown of the eastern marches; ceremonies of honor and mourning sent from the heavenly court—this too was excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo alone paid tribute yearly and stood first among the eastern vassals; that the court itself sent honors and condolences was a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 其他碌碌，咸知款貢，豈牛馬內向，東風入律者也。

translations.literal: The others are numerous and ordinary, all knowing sincere tribute—how could it be cattle and horses turning inward, the east wind entering the pitch-pipes?
translations.idiomatic: The rest were lesser peoples who knew only to offer tribute; theirs was not the turning of herds homeward nor the east wind harmonizing with the pitch-pipes of civilization.

sentences.zh: 魏正始中入寇遼西安平 三國魏志卷三０東夷傳、隋書卷八一高麗傳「遼西安平」作「西安平」。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi period of Wei they invaded Liao-xi Anping: Sanguo zhi, Wei zhi, juan 30 Dongyi zhuan and Suishu juan 81 Gaolizhuan read "Anping" for "Liao-xi Anping."
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi period of Wei they invaded Liao-xi Anping: the Dongyi zhuan in juan 30 of the Wei zhi in Sanguo zhi and the Gaolizhuan in juan 81 of Suishu read "Anping" for "Liao-xi Anping."

sentences.zh: 按後漢書郡國志二安平國屬冀州，志五，西安平屬幽州遼東郡。

translations.literal: According to Hou Hanshu, Junguo zhi 2, Anping State belonged to Jizhou; zhi 5, Xi'anping belonged to Liaodong commandery in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: According to Hou Hanshu, Junguo zhi 2, Anping State belonged to Jizhou; zhi 5, Xi'anping belonged to Liaodong commandery in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼西郡沒有安平或西安平縣。

translations.literal: Liaoxi commandery has no Anping or Xi'anping counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi commandery had no counties named Anping or Xi'anping.

sentences.zh: 這裏「遼」字衍，或「遼」下脫「東」字。

translations.literal: Here the character "Liao" is superfluous, or below "Liao" the character "dong" is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character "Liao" is superfluous, or the character "dong" has dropped out after "Liao."

sentences.zh: 正始中世宗於東堂引見其使芮悉弗 諸本「宗」作「祖」，北史卷九四高麗傳作「宣武」。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, Shizong received their envoy Ruisifu at the Eastern Hall: various editions read "zu" for "zong"; Beishi juan 94 Gaolizhuan reads "Xuanwu."
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era Emperor Shizong received their envoy Ruisifu at the Eastern Hall: various editions read "zu" for "zong"; Beishi, juan 94, Gaolizhuan, reads "Xuanwu."

sentences.zh: 按上稱「正始」年號，自當作「世宗」，北史例稱帝號。

translations.literal: According to the passage above citing the era name "Zhengshi," it should read "Shizong"; Beishi regularly uses imperial titles.
translations.idiomatic: Since the passage above cites the Zhengshi era, the text should read "Shizong"; Beishi regularly uses imperial titles.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: It is corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: It is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 具弗伏國 按卷六顯祖紀皇興元年二月、二年四月兩見此部，都作「具伏弗」。

translations.literal: Jufufu State: according to juan 6, Xianzu ji, second month of the first year of Huangxing and fourth month of the second year, this tribe appears twice, both reading "Jufufu."
translations.idiomatic: Jufufu State: according to juan 6 of the Xianzu ji, in the second month of Huangxing 1 and the fourth month of Huangxing 2, this tribe appears twice, both times as "Jufufu."

sentences.zh: 下契丹傳有「伏弗郁部」，上脫「具」字，又「郁」「部」二字倒誤，但也可證這裏「弗伏」當作「伏弗」。

translations.literal: Below in the Khitan zhuan there is "Fufu Yu tribe"; above "ju" is missing, and "yu" and "bu" are transposed in error, but this also proves that here "fufu" should read "fufu."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan account below has the "Fufu Yu tribe"; here the character "ju" is missing and "yu" and "bu" are transposed—all of which confirms that "fufu" here should read "Fufu".

sentences.zh: 拔大何國 按下契丹傳有「何大何部」，卷六顯祖紀皇興二年四月作「阿大何」。

translations.literal: Ba Dahe State: according to the Khitan zhuan below there is "He Dahe tribe"; juan 6, Xianzu ji, fourth month of Huangxing 2 reads "A Dahe."
translations.idiomatic: Ba Dahe State: the Khitan account below has "He Dahe tribe"; juan 6 of the Xianzu ji, fourth month of Huangxing 2, reads "A Dahe."

sentences.zh: 這裏「拔」字當是「何」或「阿」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "ba" should be a corruption of "he" or "a."
translations.idiomatic: Here "ba" is a corruption of "he" or "a."

sentences.zh: 地豆于國 北史卷九四「于」作「干」。

translations.literal: Didouyu State: Beishi juan 94 reads "gan" for "yu."
translations.idiomatic: Didouyu State: Beishi, juan 94, reads "gan" for "yu."

sentences.zh: 按本書他處也多作「地豆于」，間亦作「干」，北史則多作「干」，間作「于」，今仍之。

translations.literal: According to other places in this book it also mostly reads "Didouyu," sometimes "gan"; Beishi mostly reads "gan," sometimes "yu"; it is retained as is.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere in this book the name usually appears as "Didouyu," sometimes as "gan"; Beishi usually has "gan," sometimes "yu"—the text is left as it stands.

sentences.zh: 伏弗郁部羽陵部 按上勿吉傳見「具弗伏國」、「郁羽陵國」，卷六顯祖紀皇興元年二月、二年四月並見「具伏弗、郁羽陵」，這裏「伏弗」上當脫「具」字，「郁」「部」誤倒，當作「具伏弗部、郁羽陵部」。

translations.literal: Fufu Yu tribe, Yuling tribe: according to the Wuji zhuan above there appear "Jufufu State" and "Yu Yuling State"; juan 6, Xianzu ji, second month of Huangxing 1 and fourth month of Huangxing 2 both have "Jufufu, Yu Yuling"—here above "fufu" "ju" should be missing, "yu" and "bu" are wrongly reversed; it should read "Jufufu tribe, Yu Yuling tribe."
translations.idiomatic: Fufu Yu tribe, Yuling tribe: the Wuji account above has "Jufufu State" and "Yu Yuling State," and juan 6 of the Xianzu ji (Huangxing 1.2 and 2.4) has "Jufufu, Yu Yuling"—here "ju" is missing before "Fufu" and "yu" and "bu" are transposed; the text should read "Jufufu tribe, Yu Yuling tribe."

sentences.zh: 匹絜部黎部 按上勿吉傳及卷六顯祖紀皇興元年、二年並見「匹黎尒部」，通典卷二００契丹條作「匹黎部」。

translations.literal: Pijie tribe, Li tribe: according to the Wuji zhuan above and juan 6, Xianzu ji, Huangxing 1 and 2, all have "Pili'er tribe"; Tongdian juan 200, Khitan entry, reads "Pili tribe."
translations.idiomatic: Pijie tribe, Li tribe: the Wuji account and juan 6 of the Xianzu ji (Huangxing 1 and 2) all have "Pili'er tribe"; Tongdian, juan 200, Khitan entry, reads "Pili tribe."

sentences.zh: 疑這裏「匹絜」下衍「部」字，本作「匹絜黎部」，誤分二部。

translations.literal: It is suspected that below "pijie" the character "bu" is superfluous; originally it was "Pijie Li tribe," wrongly divided into two tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The character bu after "Pijie" is probably superfluous; the original was a single "Pijie Li tribe," wrongly split into two.

sentences.zh: 吐六于部 北史卷九四契丹傳「于」作「干」，卷六顯祖紀皇興二年四月作「叱六手」，通典卷二００作「比六干」。

translations.literal: Tuliuyu tribe: Beishi juan 94, Khitan zhuan, reads "gan" for "yu"; juan 6, Xianzu ji, fourth month of Huangxing 2, reads "Chiliushou"; Tongdian juan 200 reads "Biliugan."
translations.idiomatic: Tuliuyu tribe: Beishi, juan 94, Khitan zhuan, reads "gan" for "yu"; juan 6 of the Xianzu ji, fourth month of Huangxing 2, reads "Chiliushou"; Tongdian, juan 200, reads "Biliugan."

sentences.zh: 疑「吐」「比」皆「叱」字之訛。

translations.literal: It is suspected that "tu" and "bi" are both corruptions of the character "chi."
translations.idiomatic: Both "tu" and "bi" are probably corruptions of "chi."

sentences.zh: 「手」顯訛，「于」「干」不知孰是。

translations.literal: "Shou" is clearly a corruption; whether "yu" or "gan" is correct is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: "Shou" is clearly erroneous; whether "yu" or "gan" is correct cannot be determined.
